html:
Kwame Nkrumah was a Ghanaian politician who led the British Gold Coast to independence in 1957 as Ghana, the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to win it. He ruled as prime minister and then president until a coup in 1966.

He spent about twelve years studying in the United States and Britain, where he met Pan-Africanists and helped organise the Fifth Pan-African Congress in Manchester in 1945. Back home, he founded the Convention People's Party in 1949 with the slogan "Self-government now". He was jailed after a campaign of strikes and boycotts, then released when his party won the 1951 election, and became prime minister in 1952.

  • Ghana's independence on 6 March 1957 inspired movements across the continent and opened the way to the Year of Africa in 1960.
  • He was the leading voice of Pan-Africanism, calling for a united Africa, and was a founding member of the Organisation of African Unity in 1963.
  • He built schools, roads and the Akosombo Dam on the Volta River, but debts grew as cocoa prices fell.

In 1964 he made Ghana a one-party state with himself president for life. In 1966, while he was abroad on a visit to China, the army and police overthrew him. He lived in exile in Guinea and died in Bucharest in 1972. He remains a founding figure for the independent African states.
sum: Kwame Nkrumah was a Ghanaian politician who led the British Gold Coast to independence in 1957 as Ghana, the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to win it. He ruled as prime minister and then president until a coup in 1966.
